glossary.definition: The planned time between calibrations of an instrument, set by the organization and recorded in the register.

The property of a measurement result whereby it can be related to a reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing to the measurement uncertainty (NIST, adopting the VIM definition).
The list of instruments in scope with identity, owner, interval, status and attached certificates.
A calibration result outside the limits the organization accepts for the instrument.
The role accountable for decisions and records in a defined workflow.
The person who uses or looks after an instrument and answers for its condition between calibrations.
The person who checks returned evidence and decides whether the result is acceptable for the intended use.
The person who manages the calibration schedule, suppliers and register.
Fields that describe an instrument and rarely change.
Fields that describe where an instrument stands and change with events.
A description of each field, including its meaning, who fills it, allowed values and whether it can be left empty.
Evidence that a calibration event took place and produced a result, as treated in this guide.
An authorized, recorded decision to defer a calibration, with a reason and an end date.
An event that stops the normal calibration workflow.
Identifying potentially affected work, deciding what review it needs, and recording that decision.
The period from the last calibration showing the instrument within limits through its removal from service.
A planned check of equipment condition that produces a record with a result.
Maintenance that follows a schedule.
Maintenance that follows a fault or a report.
A small, controlled trial of the migration using real data before the full import.
The point at which the new register becomes the working record and the old sources stop being updated.
